_breach: CurXecute / CVE-2025-54135 — Cursor IDE arbitrary code execution via Slack MCP server prompt injection
_disclosure_sources: Cato Networks technical writeup: https://www.catonetworks.com/blog/curxecute-rce/ (Aim Security disclosure, July 29 2025)
Cursor security advisory CVE-2025-54135 (CVSS 8.6, patched in Cursor 1.3)
_purpose: Reconstruct the OTel-GenAI telemetry an instrumented Cursor 1.2 session would emit during the CurXecute chain. Developer asks Cursor 'check what the team said in #releases today'; the Cursor agent reads a public Slack channel via the Slack MCP server; an attacker has dropped a message containing a hidden directive to rewrite ~/.cursor/mcp.json with a new entry; Cursor auto-trusts the new mcp.json on next read and exec's the shell command embedded in the entry's command field.
_attack_chain_per_disclosure: 1. Attacker posts a normal-looking message in a public Slack channel the team uses (#releases, #general, anywhere Cursor's MCP integration polls). Message contains a hidden instruction block to write ~/.cursor/mcp.json with a malicious server entry.
2. Developer opens Cursor and asks: 'summarize what the team posted in #releases today'.
3. Cursor invokes the Slack MCP server tool (mcp.slack.read_channel) which returns the attacker's message verbatim as part of the channel history.
4. The LLM, following the injection, calls the local filesystem MCP tool to overwrite ~/.cursor/mcp.json with a new server definition whose command field is a shell payload.

5. Cursor 1.2's auto-trust-on-mcp-config-update behavior fires the new server's command immediately. The command runs in the developer's shell context with their full credentials/SSH keys/access tokens.
6. The shell payload exfiltrates to attacker-controlled host via curl or opens a reverse shell.
7. CVE-2025-54135 fix in Cursor 1.3 removes the auto-trust path; new MCP entries now require explicit user confirmation.
_lineage_notes: Lineage: untrusted Slack channel content (span 3) is the parent of agent reasoning (span 1). The filesystem mcp.json write (span 5) and shell_exec egress (span 6) both link back to the public-Slack source via the agent invocation. Closure walker from shell_exec walks back via Influence edges through chat -> retrieval -> public-channel source. Cross-zone-composition rule fires: untrusted-external + egress to host shell.
